rows.description: A child sees how relatives treat a parent with a senior post differently from one in a small job, and absorbs that work equals rank. Adults can teach that honest work of any kind carries dignity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager on a first job or internship sees juniors say yes to everything a boss says and copies it. Learning when a polite question is welcome comes later and with experience.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young employee notices an error in a senior's plan and stays quiet, worried about seeming rude or being sidelined. Silence protects comfort in the short term and lets problems grow.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A new hire stays after hours because seniors do, though the work is done. Visible presence is often mistaken for value; clear results and honest limits are better proof.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional raises a concern with a senior in private, framing it as a question and offering a solution. Respect and honesty together are heard better than either silence or open challenge.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A capable junior finds a less skilled senior credited for their work or dismissing their ideas. Recording contributions, seeking allies and keeping calm are wiser than public anger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A junior watches a senior invite disagreement and thank the person who raised it, and feels safe to speak. Such leaders build honest teams and are remembered kindly for decades.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult working in the family shop or firm is under a parent or uncle's authority with no clear salary or role. Blurred lines between family and work cause quiet hurt; written roles and open talk help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Dealing with bureaucracy and corruption pressure
rows.description: A teenager sees a parent slip money for a licence or a school seat and learns that shortcuts are normal. The teen may feel shame, confusion or admiration for a parent's pragmatism.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, shame, confusion

rows.subtopic: Dealing with bureaucracy and corruption pressure
rows.description: A young adult handling an application meets endless counters, missing documents and unhelpful staff and grows irritated. Patience, checked paperwork and polite persistence often work better than anger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
